title: Experimental Outcome Patchbook — 14d Goal Sprint (scratch)
body:
Purpose: quick, low-friction surface for running a 14-day micro-sprint where I treat personal goals like lightweight product experiments. Not a polished plan — scratchpad for hypothesis, measures, and small adjustments.

North-star outcome (qualitative): At the end of 14 days I feel two fewer sources of friction in my weekday routine and a clear +10% lift in focused deep-work time.

Primary success metrics (quantitative):
- Deep-focus minutes/week (baseline = 420). Target = +10% -> 462 min.
- Shippable micro-outcomes completed (defined as discrete deliverable I can demo): baseline 1/14d, target 3/14d.
- Effort-weighted velocity (EWV) = sum(outcome_score * effort_multiplier) per week. Target = 1.6x baseline.
- Attention-cost-adjusted outcome (ACAO) = outcome_value / distractions_count. Use as tie-breaker when EWV ambiguous.

Metric notes / formulas (quick):
- outcome_score = 1 (small), 2 (medium), 3 (substantial).
- effort_multiplier = 1 / (hours_spent_this_week_on_task + 0.25) to penalize runaway effort.
- EWV example: shipped doc (score 2) took 3 hours -> 2 * (1/(3+0.25)) = 0.615. Sum across week.

Signals I will log daily (very short):
- deep_minutes: number
- shippables: short title list
- focus_disruptions: count (meetings, reactive slack, urgent survs)
- mood_marker: emoji or 1-5
- friction_notes: 1-2 lines

Mini-hypotheses (explicit):
- H1: If I batch async communication into two 45-minute windows per day, deep_minutes will increase by ~20% within 1 week.
- H2: If I reserve a single 90-minute morning block labeled "single priority" then at least 2 micro-outcomes will be shipped in week 1.
- H3: If I track disruptions and proactively cancel 1 low-value recurring meeting, focus_disruptions will drop by >= 25%.

Experiments to run this sprint (concrete tweaks):
- Experiment A: No Slack pings outside 10:30–11:15 and 15:30–16:15. Auto-reply short note. (Measure: deep_minutes, focus_disruptions)
- Experiment B: Morning single-priority block 09:00–10:30 (block in calendar + 3-min pre-commit note). (Measure: shippables/week)
- Experiment C: One recurring "sync" meeting marked for cancellation review; propose agenda and move to async notes. (Measure: meeting_count, mood_marker)

Daily template (copy into daily log):
- date: 
- deep_minutes: 
- shippable_titles: 
- time_spent_on_shippables_h: 
- focus_disruptions: 
- quick-friction-note: 
- decisions-to-keep: 

Weekly check-in rubric (end of week):
- EWV delta vs baseline: (calc)
- Deep minutes delta: %
- Shippable count: #
- Clear wins (3 bullets)
- What felt expensive but low-value (3 bullets)
- One change for next week (explicit)

Retrospective prompts (end of 14d):
- Which hypothesis mostly held?
- Which small rituals stuck? Why?
- Which outcomes had the highest ACAO? (interpretation)
- If I scale this to a 28-day theme, what are top 2 priorities to double down on?
- Hard stop criteria: if deep_minutes < baseline after two weeks, revert to baseline cadence and re-run experiment with different communication windows.

Quick artifacts I want to produce (shippables):
1) "Inbox triage playbook" one-pager (30-45 min)
2) Short demo of timed batch process for weekly report (code snippet + gifs)
3) Personal 'focus dashboard' sketch (not prod, just figma wire)

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Track baseline more accurately first 3 days before labeling success.
- Try toggling the morning block to 08:00 if meetings keep bleeding into 09:00.
- Draft auto-reply template for Slack. Save under ~/snippets/slack-auto-reply.md (or linked in GH gist).
- Add a tiny chart for daily deep_minutes; manual for now (spreadsheet row).

Edge cases / watchouts:
- Meetings with external customers may be inflexible; treat as exceptions. Mark exceptions in daily log to not contaminate metric.
- Low-mood days skew deep_minutes; use mood_marker to normalize.

Signals dashboard (manual for now):
- Column A: date; B: deep_minutes; C: shippables(short); D: disruptions; E: mood; F: EWV daily; G: quick note.

Example log fragment (actual day):
- 2026-03-03: deep_minutes 78; shippables [Inbox playbook]; time_spent 0.75h; disruptions 2; mood 4; friction-note: "calendar got messy b/c I accepted ops sync"

Decisions made mid-sprint (notes):
- Move Experiment B earlier from 09:00 to 08:45 after day 2 because meetings encroached.
- Cancelled weekly "status huddle" for the sprint; replaced with two-line async thread.

Final quick thought (meta): run this like a product discovery loop: small hypothesis -> short measurement -> immediate small change. Keep friction low by preferring one-change-at-a-time. If something scales well, convert it into an explicit weekly habit and log it in my normal OKR doc.

-- end scratchpad --
